source.name: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.leaves: Foliage often conspicuously white-hairy; upper leaves and lower terminal leaflets suborbicular to reniform-cordate, 2.5–5 cm wide, coarsely crenate or undulate
records.flowers: Elongate racemes, calyces to 15 mm glabrous internally, corollas 25–35 mm; Salvia genus 2 stamens
records.habitat: Limestone rocks, cedar brakes and woodland

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial 10–40 cm from woody root, stems spreading-pilose
records.leaves: Subsessile lanceolate, to 6 × 2 cm, entire or slightly toothed
records.flowers: Floral bracts exceed calyx and calyx throat has white bristly ring (source key); calyces hispid-pilose outside; purplish-blue corolla ca. 16.5–21.5 mm; lower lip 6.5–8.5 mm with two prominent white basal areas

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Annual or short-lived perennial 20–30 cm, old plants small multi-stemmed bushy clumps, upper stems glandular-pubescent
records.leaves: 1–3(–4) cm long; lower leaves with petioles 4–18 mm (key)
records.flowers: Violet, 5–11(–13) mm corollas (key); conspicuously spreading often gland-tipped hairs on upper stems and calyces; Scutellaria calyx bears scutellum (genus)
records.fruit: Dark nutlets with overlapping lamella-like projections
records.taxonomy: 1999 flora recognizes vars. drummondii and edwardsiana distinguished by gland-tipped versus mostly eglandular lower stem hairs; hybrid/intergrade evidence with S. wrightii cited. Avoid inferring variety from species alone.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial to ca. 85(–100) cm; stems often prominent spreading/recurved pubescence (key)
records.leaves: Cordate-ovate blades to 13 cm, crenate-serrate and long-petiolate; upper leaf surfaces pubescent; abrupt change to smaller floral bracts
records.flowers: Racemes from upper nodes; bracts 4–9 × 3–6 mm; blue-violet corollas 17–23 mm with whitish lower lip; genus calyx scutellum
records.habitat: Wooded or thicketed sandy or rocky slopes
records.taxonomy: 1999 flora distinguishes subsp. bracteata from mexicana by glandular hairs on mid/lower stems; Lane 1986 questioned infraspecific divisions.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial ca. 15–20 cm; several stems from woody base; minute downcurved/appressed stem hairs requiring lens
records.leaves: Relatively small, with minute pubescence often downcurved; lower leaves sessile or with petioles to 4 mm (source key)
records.flowers: Deep violet-blue corollas 12–23 mm; calyces short-pubescent, usually lacking gland-tipped hairs; genus has scutellum
records.fruit: Black nutlets minutely evenly and closely tuberculate
records.habitat: Calcareous areas or sandy loam, prairies, slopes, open woods
records.taxonomy: Flora recognizes S. wrightii separate from S. resinosa based especially on fine direction of stem hairs; some earlier authorities lumped them.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Slender pubescent annual or biennial to 30 cm; several erect or decumbent stems
records.leaves: Ovate or oblong-ovate blades to 4 cm; lower leaf petioles nearly as long as or longer than blade, gradually reduced above; margins crenate, apex obtuse (key)
records.flowers: Few-flowered whorls with upper bracts smaller; calyx 3–5 mm; light lavender-pink, pink or bluish (rare white) corolla; 5–6 mm from key
records.taxonomy: HIGH PRIORITY: 1999 flora explicitly says Stachys agraria of authors, not Cham. & Schltdl.; Kew POWO treats Stachys crenata Raf. as tentative synonym of Stachys agraria Schltdl. & Cham. and ITIS treats auct. non usage separately. Verify specimen/circumscription before transferring facts to accepted binomial.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.leaves: Ovate to lanceolate 6–10 × 2–4 cm; lower surfaces silver-pubescent, toothed
records.flowers: Terminal spike-like racemes with silvery appressed hairs; bracts approximately as long as calyces; subsessile or pedicels <=2 mm; calyx 5–9 mm, lavender (rare white) corolla 10–18 mm, dark spots (genus key), Teucrium distinctive near one-lipped corolla and 4 stamens
records.habitat: Stream-bottom woods and low open ground

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Perennial, possibly annual, bushy herb with several stems from taproot to 70 cm
records.leaves: Median leaves mostly 3–5 lobed nearly to midrib; floral bracts 3-parted nearly to base and often longer than calyx
records.flowers: Pedicels 4–12 mm; flowering calyces 5–10 mm; corollas 6–15 mm; genus near one-lipped corolla with 4 stamens
records.taxonomy: 1999 treatment specific to var. laevigatum; var. cubense described separately with shallower median-leaf lobes and less-divided bracts. No species-wide conflation.

records.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
records.habit: Aromatic coarse annual, stems 0.2–1 m, sometimes purple
records.leaves: Ovate to suborbicular 4–15 × 3–10 cm, coarse serrate/crenate, sometimes crinkled, acute/acuminate apex; tiny glands beneath, petioles 1–8 cm
records.flowers: One-sided elongate racemes 5–15 cm of flowers singly at axils of tiny bracts; calyx 2–3 mm in bloom, elongating 8–12 mm in fruit, somewhat inflated and villous basally; white/lavender bilabiate 5-lobed corolla 2.5–3 mm; 4 stamens
records.habitat: Wet areas, low woods, streams, low pastures
records.taxonomy: 1999 flora spells epithet 'fructescens' in text, while plate and modern accepted usage are 'frutescens'; transcribed printed text faithfully and flagged probable orthographic error.
records.nativity_note: 1999 flora explicitly describes as introduced from Himalaya to East Asia

holds.reason: Not located in supplied 1999 flora; USFWS confirms native Edwards Plateau streams and narrow canyons, species morphology requires detailed authoritative treatment
